theme: Destination demand proxies: US National Park Service visitation stats API, state park attendance, museum/theme-park attendance, ski resort data, beach visitation

candidates.name: national-parks-bi
candidates.what_it_holds: national_parks_clean.csv with 18,851 monthly visitation records across 63 US National Parks, Jan 2000-Dec 2024 (300 months), star-schema with parks/dates dimension tables and a monthly visitation fact table, backed by a SQLite DB with ETL staging layer. Source stated as NPS Public Use Statistics Office (irma.nps.gov/Stats).
candidates.why_useful: Long, clean, monthly, government-sourced NPS visitation series across 63 parks (24 years) is a ready-made national-scale US leisure-travel/destination-demand proxy that could nowcast domestic NA nights alongside TSA throughput; addresses destination-demand gap adjacent to gap 10 (travel volume) and general consumer/travel strength gaps.

candidates.name: park-atlas-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Four CSVs refreshed from theparkatlas.com covering all 474 US National Park System units: parks.csv (park code, name, designation, states, 2025 visitor counts, dark-sky status, timed-entry flag, fee flag, bird species count, active alerts), entrance_fees.csv, campgrounds.csv, wildlife_checklist_counts.csv. CC0 public domain, snapshot dated 13 Sep 2026, sourced from NPS API, NPS IRMA visitation stats, NPSpecies, Recreation.gov RIDB, DarkSky.
candidates.why_useful: Actively refreshed (updated the same week as this scout run), CC0, single-year current visitor-count cross-section across all 474 NPS units plus fee/entry data; useful as an up-to-date benchmark against NPS IRMA and to sanity-check any nowcast built on the longer national-parks-bi series above.
candidates.time_coverage: single snapshot, 2025 visitor counts, refreshed Sep 2026

candidates.name: NationalParkAnnualAttendance
candidates.what_it_holds: Group project (BYU Stat 386) combining the National Parks API with a scraper ('parks_scraper.ipynb', 'nationalparksdata' package) that builds an annual-attendance dataset; includes EDA/analysis notebooks and a Streamlit app. Exact file/row counts not visible from README alone.
candidates.why_useful: A working scrape method against NPS annual attendance figures (a public, non-Airbnb source) that could be re-run for a longer or more current series than what we hold; secondary/lower confidence versus national-parks-bi since data extent is unconfirmed from the README.

candidates.name: Capstone-Disney-World-Date-and-Attendance-Predictor
candidates.what_it_holds: 12 CSVs of daily average ride wait times (resampled from 5-10 minute readings) for rides across all four Walt Disney World parks (Magic Kingdom x3, Epcot x2, Hollywood Studios x3, Animal Kingdom x4), covering Jan 2015-Dec 2021 (analysis window 2015-2019). Original data pulled from touringplans.com's public crowd-calendar dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Ride wait times are a well-established public proxy for theme-park crowd levels/attendance (touringplans.com dataset used in academic tourism-demand papers); gives a long, daily, US leisure-travel demand series independent of Airbnb, useful as a domestic discretionary-travel cross-check alongside TSA and NPS series.
candidates.size_hint: 12 CSV files, multi-year daily series per ride
candidates.license: not stated; underlying source touringplans.com is a known open dataset

candidates.name: Time-Series-Forecasting-of-Visitation-in-Skiing-Resorts
candidates.what_it_holds: Datathon project (Australian inter-university) forecasting 2026 visitor-days for 9 Australian ski resorts using Exponential Smoothing, ARIMA and RNN models; also computes a skier-satisfaction index. Underlying visitation data for the 9 resorts is part of the repo (datathon-supplied).
candidates.why_useful: One of very few public repos with an actual ski-resort visitation time series (not just US, but a genuine destination-demand dataset with methods for forecasting a seasonal leisure-travel series); low direct relevance to ABNB's US/EU markets but the modeling approach (ARIMA/ETS/RNN on visitor-days) is transferable and the raw resort data is real.

candidates.name: Disney-Time-Series-Project
candidates.what_it_holds: R Markdown project applying ARIMA, neural-net, STL+ETS, and Prophet models to Disney park attendance; repo page shows only the report PDF, .Rmd, and a Prophet HTML output -- no raw attendance CSV visible in the top-level listing.
candidates.why_useful: Method/approach reference for forecasting theme-park attendance with the same model families used elsewhere in this project (Prophet, ARIMA); low value as a data source since no committed dataset was confirmed.

candidates.name: RecreationGovAvailability
candidates.what_it_holds: Browser-console JavaScript tool (not a stored dataset) that queries the public Recreation.gov API for campsite availability at any campground ID (covers national and state park campgrounds bookable via Recreation.gov) and visualizes open dates per campsite; 16 commits, no license stated.
candidates.why_useful: Working, documented method to pull real-time camping-demand/availability signal (a leading indicator of outdoor-recreation/park demand) from a sanctioned public government API (recreation.gov), which could be adapted into a periodic pull for a national-park/state-park camping-occupancy proxy series -- currently we hold no camping-occupancy data.
candidates.geography: US, all Recreation.gov-bookable campgrounds (national + state parks)
candidates.size_hint: small script repo, no stored data
candidates.last_activity: unknown (repo shows 16 commits, date not surfaced)

candidates.name: california-national-parks-data-analysis
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps NPS visitation stats also covered by national-parks-bi and park-atlas-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Wolfram Mathematica notebook analyzing US National Park visitation trends, scoped to California parks per the repo name; exact data files not verified beyond the description.
candidates.why_useful: Possible additional NPS visitation extract scoped to California (a large ABNB market state); low confidence without confirming committed data files.

notes: The WebSearch tool's session-wide budget (200 calls, shared across all concurrent scouts) was already exhausted at the start of this run, so all queries had to go through WebFetch against api.github.com's unauthenticated search endpoint (60 req/hr, also shared/rate-limited across scouts -> several 403s and empty-result responses on multi-term queries, which needed simplifying to 2-3 keywords). No gh CLI was used, per instructions. Coverage gaps versus the theme brief: could not get usable results for 'museum attendance', 'beach visitation', or 'state park attendance' specifically -- GitHub search kept returning 0 items or 403s for those terms; a re-run once the rate limit resets, or with the browser (claude-in-chrome) to hit github.com's UI search directly, would likely surface more (e.g. Smithsonian visitor stats, US state-park-system annual reports, county beach-counter programs). The strongest real find is national-parks-bi (63-park, 24-year monthly NPS series, committed CSV) plus park-atlas-data (all-474-unit current snapshot, CC0, actively refreshed) -- both should be checked against the NPS IRMA site directly since our own team likely has easier direct access to irma.nps.gov than to these secondary GitHub copies, but the GitHub copies save the scrape/format work. The Disney ride-wait-time data (touringplans.com mirror) is a genuine, previously-used-in-academia demand proxy worth a look if the team wants a domestic-leisure cross-check beyond TSA throughput.
